Stripe's official docs set the global limit at 100 requests per second in live mode and 25 per second in sandbox (the docs' term for test mode). Individual endpoints default to 25 per second, and some resources have stricter limits.

- **Live mode:** The global limit is 100 requests per second per account, and the docs say to treat limits as maximums. (Live mode is for when you're ready to launch your app, and the global API rate limit there is 100 requests per second.)
- **Test/sandbox mode:** The global limit is 25 requests per second. (The sandbox global limit is 25 requests per second.)
- **Per-endpoint default:** API endpoints have a default limit of 25 requests per second.
- **Stricter resource limits:** The Files API allows 20 read and 20 write requests per second, and the Search API allows 20 read requests per second (Files API and Payouts API limits are listed in the rate-limits table, with Search at 20 read operations per second).
- **Exceeding limits:** Requests over the limit return 429 Too Many Requests HTTP status responses.

Some secondary sources differ. One says the live limit is 100 parallel requests per second for live mode transactions, and 25 parallel requests per second for test mode transactions. Another describes 100 read operations and 100 write operations per second in live mode, with test mode at 25 each. The official rate-limits page is the authoritative reference, and the figures above match it.

content.text:
Stripe's rate-limits page gives these defaults. My direct fetch of the page was refused, so these figures come from a search summary of it. Check the page before you rely on them.

| Scope | Default limit |
|---|---|
| Live mode, global | 100 requests/second |
| Sandbox (test mode), global | 25 requests/second |
| Per endpoint | 25 requests/second |
| Files API | 20 reads/second and 20 writes/second |
| Search API | 20 reads/second |

- Requests over a limit get an HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` response.
- Some resources have stricter limits than the defaults. The Payouts API is one of them, but I didn't get its numbers.
- Some third-party sources describe the live limit differently, for example as 100 reads and 100 writes per second. I'd go with Stripe's own page.

Sources:
- [Stripe rate limits](https://docs.stripe.com/rate-limits)
- [Stripe rate limits (markdown)](https://docs.stripe.com/rate-limits.md)
- [Stripe Support: rate_limit error](https://support.stripe.com/questions/rate-limit-error)
